healer.no_public_base: His own site gives only his native city (Los Angeles) and his role at the University of Arizona's SEMA Lab; it does not say where he lives or is based. The Unified Mindfulness company address (Charlotte, Vermont) is the organisation's, not his.

create.name: Shinzen Young
create.bio:
Shinzen Young is an American meditation teacher known for a precise, almost engineering-like way of teaching mindfulness, which he has organised into a system called Unified Mindfulness. Raised in Los Angeles, he was drawn to Japan as a teenager, studied Asian languages at UCLA and went on to doctoral work in Buddhist studies, during which he spent three years as a monk in the Shingon school on Mount Koya and received the name Shinzen. A friendship there with the Jesuit writer William Johnston widened his interest to the mystical traditions of many faiths and to the scientific study of meditation.

His teaching breaks experience down into seeing, hearing and feeling, and trains concentration, sensory clarity and equanimity through a large menu of named techniques that students can mix to suit their temperament. He often explains meditative states with maths and science metaphors, and he works with researchers in contemplative neuroscience, including as co-director of a lab at the University of Arizona. He leads a weekly Life Practice Program by phone and online, in which he coaches a student live, and his methods are taught by a network of certified Unified Mindfulness coaches. His book The Science of Enlightenment sets out the whole approach.

books.title: The Science of Enlightenment: How Meditation Works
books.author: Shinzen Young
books.description: His full account of how meditation works, written in plain language with stories from his years as a monk. It explains his core skills of concentration, clarity and equanimity and maps them onto the major contemplative traditions.

courses.title: Shinzen Young's Life Practice Program
courses.description: A monthly subscription to a weekly one-hour call in which Shinzen leads short guided meditations and coaches a fellow practitioner on bringing practice into daily life. Subscribers can also stream the full archive.

courses.title: Unified Mindfulness Teacher Certification
courses.description: A staged training in teaching his system, from a self-paced online foundation course to live small-group classes, a supervised practicum and a year-long trainer programme.

free_resources.title: Shinzen Young Resources
free_resources.description: A free collection on his site of articles, videos and practice material introducing his approach to meditation, with links to his book and training.

flags: No hub (Kripalu, Esalen, Omega, IMS) named as a place he teaches on his own site; listed without a hub link.
No personal email published: only programme inboxes (support@lifepracticeprogram.com, hpp@unifiedmindfulness.com) appear on his retreat schedule, so the contact form is used.
shinzen.org asks for a 10-second crawl delay and unifiedmindfulness.com 60 seconds; both were respected.
Unified Mindfulness is a separate company (UM-HUB LLC) teaching his system; the teacher certification is listed as his offering because his site sends students there.
Several of his most-viewed videos fail oEmbed (embedding disabled, HTTP 401) and were left out.
Book ISBN from the Amazon/IndieBound links on his resources page, not confirmed elsewhere.
Health rule: his newest book (with Shelly Young) and Natural Pain Relief are condition-led and left out; the rest of his work is general meditation teaching.
left_out: When Therapy Doesn't Work: A Mindfulness Guide to Emotional Repair (book): sold on trauma, anxiety and addiction.
Home Practice Program weekend retreats: led mostly by Unified Mindfulness coaches, not by him.
Audio downloads in his store (e.g. Calming the Mind, $5.99): no individual product pages, only add-to-cart buttons.
Brightmind app: created by another teacher (Toby Sola), only promoted on his site.
Embedded-disabled videos: Welcome to New Viewers, Tea Coffee and Meditation, What to Expect After a Retreat, and others.
